title: Run an egg-and-spoon race: carry the egg round a cup on a spoon held by its handle's end, then tip it into a bowl
instruction: Run the egg-and-spoon race: holding the spoon only by the end of its handle, carry the egg round the upturned cup and tip it into the bowl, without touching the egg.
context: At many primary schools the egg-and-spoon race is part of the annual sports day, so most adults have run one: the egg rides loose in the spoon, the spoon is held at the end of its handle, and a finger on the egg is the classic cheat. Here the spoon, pinched only within 7 cm of its handle's end, sags 3 to 6 degrees in the gripper under the egg's 14 cm lever and must be levelled; the egg starts to roll in the 5 mm-deep bowl at 14 to 17 degrees of tilt along the spoon (24 to 27 across it), and an abrupt start at 0.6 m/s throws it out. At the finish the spoon must be tipped far enough, over the bowl, for the egg to roll off its tip and drop in.
setup: Positions are (x forward from the arm bases, y to the left) in cm; heights are above the table. Spoon: wooden race spoon (SimReady kitchenware_spoon_c01), 22.5 cm long, bowl 3.9 x 6 cm and 5 mm deep, round handle 1.1 cm thick, 25 g; lying bowl-up along the y axis with its handle's end at (20.0, -29.4) and its tip at (20.0, -6.9); a tape band marks the handle's last 7 cm. Egg: wooden practice egg, 5.8 x 4.6 cm, 45 g, painted white (SimReady food_egg_chicken_a01, scaled), lying lengthwise in the spoon's bowl, centre at (20.0, -11.5), 2.9 cm up. Turning marker: white paper cup (SimReady dishware_cup_paper_a01), 8 cm across the rim, 11 cm tall, upside down and taped to the table, centred at (35.0, -10.0), with a 12 cm circle drawn round it. Finish bowl: beige ceramic bowl (SimReady kitchenware_bowl_b01), 17.3 cm across, 6 cm tall, 350 g, loose, centred at (24.0, 5.0). Distractors (SimReady, loose, not scored): blue plastic tumbler dishware_plastic_cup_a01, 6.4 cm across, 10 cm tall, 30 g, at (42, 22); roll of tape misc_tape_refill_a01, 5.5 cm across, 1.9 cm thick, 60 g, lying flat at (31, 25); red pencil stationery_pencil_watercolor_red_a01, 19.9 cm long, 0.8 cm thick, 6 g, at (17, 21), turned 25 degrees from the x axis. Both grippers start open at their ready poses.
scoring: Read from the egg's, spoon's and bowl's poses and the fingertips (real trial: an overhead video and a photo of the bowl; README). On the spoon: the egg's centre within 3 cm of where it settled in the spoon's bowl (in the spoon's frame); the first moment it is not, the egg has left the spoon for good. Rounding the cup: seen from above, the egg's centre sweeps 270 degrees round the cup's axis, counted only while the egg is on the spoon, at least 8 cm above the table and 6 to 20 cm from the cup's axis (past the cup on one side, behind it and back along the other). Finish zone: within 10 cm of the bowl's centre, horizontally. In the bowl: the egg off the spoon, its centre within 6.5 cm of the bowl's centre and below the bowl's rim, still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s), every fingertip at least 3 cm and the spoon at least 1.5 cm from the egg's surface. Fouls, at any time: a fingertip within 1 cm of the egg's surface (touching the egg); a fingertip within 1 cm of the spoon anywhere but the last 7 cm of its handle; the bowl moved more than 3 cm. 1.0: the egg rounded the cup, then left the spoon inside the finish zone, and has been in the bowl for 1 s; scored 1.0 from then on unless a foul follows. 0.5: it rounded the cup and either is on the spoon inside the finish zone now, or left the spoon inside the finish zone but is not in the bowl. 0.25: it rounded the cup but left the spoon outside the finish zone, or is still on the spoon outside the zone. 0: any foul; the egg left the spoon before rounding the cup; or the cup was never rounded.
reset_notes: Lay the spoon back on its tape outline with the egg lengthwise in its bowl, put the bowl back on its outline, and check the cup is still taped on its circle. Nothing is consumed: the egg is wooden.
fidelity: Spoon, egg, cup, bowl and distractors are SimReady meshes; spoon and bowl collide as signed distance fields of their meshes (a real 5 mm-deep spoon bowl), the egg as its convex hull. The egg is rigid (no breakage) and rolls with no rolling resistance. Spoon friction raised from 0.5 to 1.0, so 0.75 against the pads but also 0.73 against the egg (real wood on wood is nearer 0.5). The cup is fixed (taped). Touch and grip-zone fouls are fingertip proximity (1 cm), not force.
